title: The last day of May
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The last day of May. Nothing happens. Wood draws the seawall, the bay, the dog. A strip about nothing happening in a town where nothing does. The owner will say it's the best one. The strip agrees and doesn't understand why.

panels.composition: The seawall at the end of main street, late afternoon, the bay flat. WOOD sitting on the wall. BARNABY beside him. Nothing else.

image.prompt: a young man and a small dog sitting on a low concrete seawall above a flat gray bay in late afternoon light, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The same. The light a little lower.

image.prompt: the same young man and dog on a seawall with the light a little lower, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The same. A gull, far off. The dog's ear.

image.prompt: the same seawall scene with a distant gull and the small dog's ear lifted, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The same. The gull gone. The dog's ear down. The strip's fourth panel is a man and a dog on a wall and nothing happened and it's the best one.

image.prompt: the same young man and dog on a seawall with the gull gone and the light nearly gone, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Four panels of nothing. The strip's first deliberate one. (The Rain, Jan 14, was the first silent.)
